title: Tenali Raman and the Shadow of the Gold Coins

full_text:
A wealthy and merciless moneylender named Dhaniram took advantage of an impoverished traveling merchant named Madhava.
During a sweltering summer noon, Madhava, exhausted and faint from heat, sat down to rest for an hour in the cool shade cast by the wall of Dhaniram’s mansion.
When Madhava stood up to resume his journey, Dhaniram ran out and demanded five silver coins!
'Thou didst use the shade of my private mansion wall to cool thy body!' shouted Dhaniram. 'The shade belongs to my property; pay for the shadow or I will have the guards seize thy baggage!'

The poor merchant was stunned, having no money.
Tenali Raman, who was passing by, witnessed the extortion.
Tenali stepped forward:
'Dhaniram is legally correct! Property rights must be respected! Let us settle this account before King Krishnadevaraya.'

They went to the royal court.
Dhaniram presented his claim: 'Maharaj, the merchant consumed the cool shadow of my wall; he must pay five silver coins!'
The King frowned, disgusted by the usurer’s shameless greed, but struggled to find a legal precedent.

Tenali Raman smiled:
'Maharaj, I shall settle the payment immediately on behalf of the poor traveler.'

Tenali had a large, polished silver tray placed upon the sunny courtyard floor.
Tenali took five bright silver coins from his own purse and arranged them in a row upon the edge of the tray.
The bright midday sun cast the dark, distinct shadows of the five silver coins across the surface of the silver tray!

Tenali pointed to the tray and said:
'Master Dhaniram, step forward and receive your payment!
The traveler used the shadow of your wall to cool himself; he did not remove a single brick, stone, or drop of mortar from your house.
Therefore, it is only just that you take the shadow of these five silver coins to enrich your purse!
Reach out your hands, scoop up the five shadows from the tray, and take them home to your treasury!'

The court erupted in thunderous applause and laughter!
Dhaniram stood humiliated, unable to pick up a shadow.
He stammered: 'I cannot pick up a shadow!'

Tenali replied with ringing moral authority:
'If you cannot pick up a shadow of money, how dare you charge real silver for the shadow of a wall?
Heaven made the sun and the shade for all living creatures. Whosoever charges money for cool air and shade is a thief of nature’s bounty!'

King Krishnadevaraya fined the greedy moneylender fifty silver coins for harassing travelers, and Tenali’s witty justice was celebrated throughout the capital.
moral: Extortionate usurers who demand payment for non-existent services must be repaid with the shadows of money.
